first_impression.reaction: I googled 'wedding centrepieces' after another hour on Pinterest, expecting a listicle of 50 mason jars. The first line is me: I do have a hundred saved photos and most wouldn't work on our tables. No 'dream day', no 'fairytale'. It promises a way to choose before the gallery, so I kept going. The height rule and the destination questions are the bits I'd actually use. It's a styling post, so I'm not booking anyone off it, but it doesn't feel tacky.

journey.quote: The piece that stops you scrolling was styled for one room, one table shape and one light.
journey.reaction: Fair point, and not one I'd thought about. Feels like someone who has actually set a room.

journey.quote: The middle height, a solid wall of flowers at face level, is the one to avoid.
journey.reaction: This is the thing I'd get wrong. At James's cousin's wedding we talked to a hydrangea all night. Clear, practical, done.

journey.quote: A single tall piece on a long table looks marooned.
journey.reaction: Honest trade-off, nicely put. Helps me throw out half my board.

journey.quote: Stems are the expensive part of most arrangements, so the levers are about using fewer of them well:
journey.reaction: Useful levers, but no sense of what flowers for 8 or 9 tables actually costs. I get it's linked elsewhere; Dad will still ask.

journey.quote: Move ceremony arrangements to the reception rather than buying twice.
journey.reaction: Smart, and later the page admits someone has to physically carry them during drinks. That's the honest follow-through I like.

journey.quote: *Suits:* round tables in courtyards, gardens and smaller dining rooms.
journey.reaction: The 'Suits' line on every idea is what makes this better than Pinterest. I skimmed most of the 30 just reading those.

journey.quote: Each table can hold a different chapter.
journey.reaction: Slightly twee. Books and photos of us on every table is the kind of thing our friends would quietly smirk at. Not a deal-breaker.

journey.quote: Where the venue restricts open flame, battery-operated candles keep the glow, and they are a good and safe alternative to traditional candles.
journey.reaction: Fine info, but this sentence reads like a fire brigade leaflet pasted in. Clunky next to the rest.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, so these details are settled before anything is booked.
journey.reaction: Good. Inclusions in writing speaks straight to my hidden-costs worry.

journey.quote: When you cannot visit the florist's studio, the right questions do the work. Take these to the venue and to a local florist.
journey.reaction: Great questions, genuinely insider stuff (who does pack-down, keeping flowers fresh outdoors). But it hands the job back to us. We don't want to spend our evenings emailing a florist in another time zone; that's why we'd hire someone.

journey.quote: A video call walking through a sample centrepiece is often worth more than any number of photos.
journey.reaction: Practical, specific tip. Would never have thought to ask for that.

journey.section: Planning the table with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, start to finish.
journey.reaction: Every planner says start to finish. What does that mean for flowers specifically: do you find the florist, or do we? Who's in the room at set-up?

unanswered_questions: Roughly what do centrepieces cost per table for 60 to 90 guests, even as a range or via the linked flowers cost guide?
Is there a real wedding (venue and date) showing any of these centrepieces in place?
When you say the Wedded Advisor plans vendors, do you find and brief the local florist, or do we? (deferred business detail)
Who is physically there at set-up and pack-down on the day? (deferred business detail)
How does Wedded Wonderland charge for this, and are there commissions from florists or hire companies? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: Take these to the venue and to a local florist.
turn_offs_found.why: Puts the legwork on us. We're paying to avoid exactly this, and it leaves it unclear whether the Advisor does it or we do.

turn_offs_found.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, start to finish.
turn_offs_found.why: Reads as the generic end-to-end claim every planner makes, with nothing on who is accountable on the day.

would_share_with: James: the 'Height and sightlines' section and 'Table shape', so we can agree on long versus round before we argue about flowers
My mum: the 'Centrepieces for a destination wedding' questions, because she'll want to know who handles the flowers overseas

cta_reaction.quote: Begin the conversation with our [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-centrepieces&utm_content=closing) team.
cta_reaction.why: Soft, no pressure, which I like. But it's a styling post and we haven't picked a destination. I'd bookmark it, read a couple more posts and want to see a real wedding before enquiring.

top_3_changes: Stop handing the destination legwork back to us. Old: "Take these to the venue and to a local florist." New: "Take these to the venue and to a local florist, or work through them with your Wedded Advisor."

Smooth the safety sentence so it doesn't read like a leaflet. Old: "battery-operated candles keep the glow, and they are a good and safe alternative to traditional candles." New: "battery-operated candles keep the glow and are a safe alternative to traditional candles."
Tone down the twee line. Old: "Each table can hold a different chapter." New: "Keep it to one or two pieces per table so it feels personal rather than staged."

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Sophie & James (planner couple): skimmed, looked for practical insider detail, hidden costs, accountability and tackiness risk
No invented brand facts; fees, commissions, supplier sourcing and on-the-day presence listed as deferred unanswered questions
Suggested edits use exact old strings from the draft and add no new facts or measurements
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored

open_questions.question: Is there an existing real Wedded Wonderland wedding post with venue and date that could be linked from the centrepiece ideas? This couple wants one before enquiring.

assumptions: Sophie & James arrived via a Google search for 'wedding centrepieces' while early in research with no destination chosen, so relevance is 3 and enquiry likelihood 2 (they enquire after 2 to 3 posts plus a real wedding).
Fees, commissions, supplier sourcing and vetting are deferred by the brand and not penalised as must-fix; suggested edits stay within existing page claims.
Fast-mode read: read intro, how-to-choose, practical details, destination section and close in full; skimmed the 30 ideas mainly via their 'Suits' lines; FAQ skimmed.
